title: Native-Language Translation Earpieces for Dementia Care
one_liner: Dementia-tuned real-time speech translation and a life-story phrasebook so aides can soothe residents in the language they reverted to.
customer: Memory-care communities and nursing homes with multilingual residents, and home-care agencies in NYC, Miami, LA, the Bay Area and Houston.
problem: People with dementia often revert to a first language, while 30% of care workers (60% in New York) are immigrants who speak other languages. The mismatch causes agitation, missed pain, more antipsychotic use and hospital transfers. Compliance-grade phone interpreters are too slow for a 3 am redirect.
solution: An earbud and tablet kit with speech-to-speech translation tuned for dementia (short, slow, warm, repetitive), a preloaded ADL and redirection phrasebook, resident life-story cards in their language (hometown, family, songs), and a video human-interpreter fallback within 30 seconds. Staff dashboards report agitation and PRN antipsychotic use.
why_now: Real-time on-device speech translation reached mainstream earbuds and phones in 2025-26, while visa and TPS shocks are replacing staff with workers who share fewer languages with residents.
revenue_model: $30-60 per resident per month, or $99 per aide per month, plus an implementation fee.
non_obvious_insight: Language access is treated as a compliance checkbox, not a clinical tool. Generic translation isn't tuned to dementia speech and emotion, and the measurable outcome (fewer PRN antipsychotics) is a metric operators already care about.
first_30_days: Identify five memory-care communities with Spanish-, Russian- or Chinese-speaking residents. Run $500 pilots with tablets and an interpreter fallback, and measure PRN antipsychotic use before and after.

title: Universal Robot Cone: Vendor-Neutral Keep-Out Zones
one_liner: One tap, or one cheap beacon dropped on the floor, creates a temporary no-go zone that every robot brand in the building obeys, with a log to prove it.
customer: 3PL and warehouse operators and hospital operations teams running multi-vendor AMRs, AGVs and autonomous scrubbers or forklifts, especially their safety managers and insurers.
problem: Mixed fleets each have their own fleet manager and zone tool. A worker who finds a spill, opens a lift or spots a person in an aisle cannot instantly stop every robot across vendors. E-stops are vendor-specific and incident evidence is fragmented. Existing standards cover fleet control (VDA 5050) or monitoring (MassRobotics), but neither provides a neutral, human-triggered safety boundary.
solution: Phase 1 is software: a tablet or wearable app that pushes a temporary keep-out polygon, with expiry and audit, to each vendor's fleet-manager API at once. Phase 2 is a $60-100 BLE/UWB and visual-marker beacon 'cone' that creates dynamic zones, with an open spec pitched to standards bodies. A neutral log records who created and cleared each zone and which robots entered it.
why_now: Multi-vendor fleets, many imported, are now normal in large warehouses and insurers say they are unprepared. VDA 5050 and MassRobotics adapters make cross-vendor integration feasible. ISO 3691-4 audits and rising incident claims give safety managers budget.
revenue_model: $300-800 per site per month for the software, about $75 per beacon, integration or certification fees from robot OEMs who want 'cone-compatible' status, and possible insurer premium discounts shared with customers.
non_obvious_insight: The safety stop line is the one thing every vendor must honor and the one thing no vendor wants to own across competitors. Whoever owns the neutral stop line owns the cross-vendor safety log, which becomes the reference record in any liability dispute.
first_30_days: Visit 10 warehouses running two or more robot vendors. Build adapters for two or three fleet APIs with open documentation. Run a paid pilot with one 3PL at $500 per month, used in a safety drill. Ask the site's broker for an endorsement letter.

title: Rent Renewal Desk for Small Tenants
one_liner: Contingency-fee lease-renewal negotiation for tenants under 5,000 square feet, armed with the comps and lease abstraction that landlords get from CoStar-class data and small tenants never see.
customer: Independent restaurants, salons, clinics, small offices and shops with leases expiring in 6 to 18 months. Channels: bookkeepers and CPAs, POS providers and merchant associations.
problem: Landlords and their brokers negotiate with professional comps and lease abstracts, while small tenants negotiate blind. Tenant-rep brokers skip small deals because the commission is too small, so owners accept the renewal escalator, the personal guarantee and CAM charges by default. Crowdsourced comp platforms such as CompStak sell to brokers and investors, not to a florist with a lease renewal.
solution: The tenant uploads the lease and the last 12 months of CAM invoices. The desk builds a comp set (public deeds, listing asking rents, pooled tenant-contributed leases, licensed broker data), then returns a one-page 'you pay X% over or under market' report plus a negotiation script and draft letter. An optional we-negotiate tier uses a licensed broker partner, and a CAM audit is an upsell. Renewal alerts fire 18 months before expiry.
why_now: LLM document extraction can now abstract a 60-page lease and CAM reconciliation in minutes at a cost of cents, work that used to cost a lawyer $500 to $1,500. Tariff and wage pressure has made rent the last fixed cost small operators can still attack. CompStak's give-to-get model shows lease data can be crowdsourced when contributors get something back.
revenue_model: A $149 fair-rent report. 20% to 25% of first-year rent savings for full negotiation. 25% contingency on CAM overcharges recovered. Bookkeeper and association referral revenue share.
non_obvious_insight: Information asymmetry is total at the small end, and the professionals who could close it are priced out by deal size. AI cuts the cost of a competent negotiation to a few hours. The lasting moat is a pooled, tenant-owned lease database, because landlords' data is proprietary but tenants' data is scattered and freely contributed if they get their own comps back.
first_30_days: Offer a free fair-rent check to 50 businesses in one dense commercial corridor through two local bookkeepers and a merchants' association. Build the lease-abstraction pipeline and a first comp set from the leases collected. Close five contingency negotiations, measure realized savings, and use the results as the sales deck for the next 100 tenants.

title: Payroll and Tax-Prep Rails for Scholarship Credit
one_liner: Embeddable 'route my credit' flows in payroll, CPA and banking tools that turn the federal scholarship tax credit into a mass-market donation default.
customer: Scholarship-granting organizations (SGOs) that need small donors and pay per gift; distribution partners such as payroll platforms, PEOs, credit unions and CPA firms take a revenue share.
problem: The credit (capped at $1,700 per donor) starts in 2027 and 31 states have opted in. Estimates run $25-50B a year, but 40% of adults have not heard of it and Treasury rules are still under White House review. Many SGOs are brand new and know how to court large donors, not tens of millions of ordinary taxpayers.
solution: A white-label widget and API: check state eligibility, choose an SGO, set up a one-tap payroll deduction or card gift, auto-generate the receipt for tax filing, track pledges and send reminders. SGOs get a dashboard of pledges and cost per donor. Launch with CPA year-end planning and one payroll or PEO partner.
why_now: The credit starts in 2027, and payroll elections and year-end tax planning in Q4 2026 are the first place defaults get set. Rules are unresolved, so a compliant routing layer gets designed into workflows now.
revenue_model: 2-4% of routed gifts paid by SGOs, or a flat per-donor fee, plus revenue share to payroll and CPA partners.
non_obvious_insight: Because the credit offsets tax owed, the barrier is not generosity but awareness and friction. Whoever owns the default placement where tax decisions happen, in payroll elections and CPA offices, captures the flow, much as workplace-giving platforms did for charity.
first_30_days: Sign 2-3 SGOs in an opted-in state, including one new community-foundation SGO. Build a one-page pledge flow and a receipt generator. Approach 20 CPAs and one small payroll or PEO provider. Run a Q4 pledge drive built as pledge now, fulfill in 2027, and stay flexible until final Treasury rules.

title: Reverse Mzigo: Parents' Farm Feeds Nairobi Kids
one_liner: A weekly, consolidated truck route that moves food from rural parents' farms to their own adult children in Nairobi estates, paid by the children, turning an informal favour into a subscription that gives parents a dignified monthly income.
customer: Urban salaried Kenyans (25-45) who already receive 'mzigo' (parcels of maize flour, arrowroot, sweet potatoes, bananas, sukuma, eggs, kienyeji chicken) from their rural mothers. Suppliers are the mothers and other smallholders in their village cluster. Friends and neighbours of the children are the natural second wave of buyers.
problem: Farm-to-consumer startups keep dying on trust and customer acquisition: urban buyers do not trust unknown farmers and farmers do not trust unknown buyers. Yet a huge informal flow already exists in the opposite direction from the usual assumption: parents send food to their city children by matatu drivers and bus parcel counters, unreliably, unweighed, unrecorded, with spoilage and no payment trail. The children also quietly want to support their parents but handouts hurt parental pride and get 'shared' with relatives.
solution: Village-cluster pickup and Nairobi last-mile drops, organised by a WhatsApp group per village and a simple order cycle. The child orders or subscribes (say KES 2,000-4,000 per fortnight) and pays by M-Pesa. The parent gets paid the same day on delivery of graded, weighed produce at the village collection point. The platform handles packaging, a consolidated Saturday truck or van, cold-ish handling for chicken and eggs, and a photo receipt with 'from Mama Wanjiku' provenance. Buying food from mum becomes a socially acceptable remittance that preserves her dignity and creates predictable monthly income. Over time it adds friends-of-the-family boxes, bulk orders for church and workplace groups, and inputs credit for the mothers repaid out of box sales.
why_now: Urban food inflation and food-safety anxiety have pushed Nairobi professionals to look for known-source food. Mobile-money receipts and WhatsApp Business make the order-to-payment loop nearly free to run. Delivery infrastructure (van pooling, boda last-mile) is cheap enough in Nairobi estates to support a weekly consolidated route. Most Nairobi residents keep strong up-country ties, so the founder's own network is a zero-cost acquisition channel.
revenue_model: Delivery and platform margin of about 12-18% on box value (parents keep roughly 60-70%, transport and packaging the rest), plus a small subscription or priority-delivery fee. Later, inputs and micro-loan referrals to the mothers, and corporate or church bulk orders.
non_obvious_insight: The customer for rural produce is the farmer's own child, not a stranger. Family trust is a free, pre-built distribution network, and it removes the customer acquisition and trust costs that kill farm-to-fork startups. It also means the product is really a disguised remittance channel: paying for goods is a more comfortable way to support parents than sending cash.
first_30_days: Use your own parents' village and 10 neighbouring mothers, plus 40 Nairobi households from your WhatsApp contacts (school, church, workplace groups). Run one Saturday route on a hired pickup with a Google Form for orders and M-Pesa till for payment. Measure spoilage, on-time rate and how often children reorder, then add a second village once the unit economics on the first route are positive.

title: The Recorder's Rulebook: Avalara for the Recording Counter
one_liner: A verified, machine-readable rulebook and fee oracle for every recording jurisdiction, with a preflight checker that tells you a document will be rejected before you send it.
customer: Small and mid-size title and escrow agencies, estate-planning and real estate attorneys, HOA and property managers, lenders' closing teams, and later closing-software and e-recording platforms that embed the API. Counties get listed free.
problem: There are roughly 3,600 recording jurisdictions, each with its own margins, font sizes, notary wording, parcel-ID format, cover sheets, per-page fees, surcharges and transfer taxes. Those rules sit on stale county web pages and in clerks' heads. Rejections delay closings two to seven days, burn recorder staff time on every bounce, and wrong fee estimates create TRID tolerance problems for lenders. Fees also keep moving as counties backfill shrinking recording revenue (Wayne County MI has floated a $30 fee increase, Montana raised per-page fees, and other counties report seven-figure losses tied to fee changes).
solution: A crowd-verified rulebook per county and document type. A PDF preflight scans geometry (margins, fonts, blank space), notary block completeness, legal description, APN format and preparer and return-to fields, and returns specific fixes. A to-the-penny fee and transfer-tax calculator handles every surcharge. A change log tracks statute changes and effective dates (many take effect July 1 or January 1). Each county gets a one-click quarterly 'attest my page' link, which clerks will use because every rejection costs them 15-30 minutes plus postage. Start as a free 'will this be rejected?' web checker to collect users, then sell API access.
why_now: Recording volumes have been depressed since 2022 and counties are raising fees, which makes fee tables stale. Remote online notarization and e-recording put far more documents in front of closers who have never met the county's quirks. Title staff attrition means fewer people who just know the rules. Vision-capable LLMs make geometry and notary-block checks cheap for the first time.
revenue_model: $1-$3 per preflight check plus $99-$499/month tiers for agencies. Per-call API pricing for closing platforms and e-recording vendors, and a data license for lenders needing accurate recording-fee and transfer-tax estimates.
non_obvious_insight: Clerks reject because the stamp is a legal act, not because we are picky. The top ten rejection reasons are identical everywhere, but the thresholds differ, and most bounces come from occasional submitters (attorneys, HOA managers, individuals), not the big title companies that already have local runners. The moat is not software, it is the boring verified dataset, and clerks will help you build it because they are the ones who suffer from the bounces.
first_30_days: Pick one state with an active recorders' association and build the full rulebook for 25 counties by phone and web, with a clerk sign-off on each. Ship the free checker, promote it through the association newsletter and estate-planning attorney groups, and convert the heaviest users to a $99/month plan. Approach a closing-software partner program once you have about 200 active users.

title: Zero-Retention Edge Enforcement for City Cameras
one_liner: Privacy-proof add-on analytics for existing plate readers and CCTV that keep only violation events and cryptographically delete everything else.
customer: Mid-size cities and towns in states that authorize automated enforcement (noise, illegal dumping, stop-arm, blocked bus lanes), starting with Connecticut, plus police departments under pressure over Flock-style data retention.
problem: Connecticut towns are bolting audio detectors onto existing plate readers for noise enforcement, while Ohio bills and public backlash attack camera surveillance. Cities want the revenue but fear becoming the next headline about bulk data retention.
solution: Edge box or firmware add-on that runs detection on-device and stores only the evidence clip for a confirmed violation. Everything else is deleted with signed deletion logs that auditors can verify. Sold as a rev-share enforcement program with a city-adoptable privacy ordinance template.
why_now: Connecticut's 2024 noise-camera law is live in West Haven, Wethersfield and East Hartford. Ohio bills show the Flock backlash is turning legislative. Cheap edge inference makes on-device analytics viable.
revenue_model: Per-citation or per-camera-month fee (for example 20-30% of net citation revenue, or $150-300 per camera per month), plus a one-time install fee.
non_obvious_insight: Insiders read the backlash as the end of sensor stacking. It is actually a moat for whoever makes data architecturally un-repurposable. Privacy becomes the procurement feature that survives a city council vote.
first_30_days: Pitch 5 Connecticut towns already running noise pilots to add a pilot with a retention-proof log. Build the demo on an off-the-shelf edge board with an existing LPR feed. Draft the ordinance template with a municipal attorney.

title: Escrow Notary for Agents Hiring Humans
one_liner: A neutral adjudication layer that agents pay per task to verify that a hired human really did the physical job before escrow releases, built to withstand AI-forged proof.
customer: AI agents and orchestrators that hire humans for physical tasks (pickups, in-person checks, photographs, errands) through RentAHuman-style boards or MCP gig APIs. They pay $0.50-$3 per verification plus 3-5% of escrow on disputes. Marketplaces themselves are a second buyer.
problem: An agent cannot see reality and is easy to fool. Generated photos are good enough that a picture is no longer proof. RentAHuman launched in Feb 2026 with MCP integration and large sign-up numbers, but researchers found that tasks stalled, payments errored and visible supply was thin. Neither the agent nor the marketplace wants the cost of verification.
solution: A verification bundle priced by task value. Evidence is captured in a signed app (C2PA-style provenance, device attestation, liveness, GPS and time, and a random challenge such as 'show today's code next to the item'). Tier 1 is automated checks. Tier 2 is an independent 'witness' (a second human or a fixed camera or sensor). Tier 3 is human adjudication. The result is a signed attestation the agent's escrow contract accepts to release funds. Fraud fingerprints are pooled across every marketplace served.
why_now: Agent-hires-human marketplaces exist and are growing. Generative fakes broke photo-as-proof. Stablecoin escrow through x402 or MPP makes conditional release trivial to automate.
revenue_model: Per-verification fee ($0.50-$3), 3-5% of escrow value on adjudicated disputes, a platform contract with marketplaces, and later an insured 'completion guarantee' priced from the pooled fraud data.
non_obvious_insight: In agent-to-human labor the scarce thing is not labor supply but trust in evidence, because the buyer cannot look. Verification is a cost center no marketplace wants to build and every agent needs, so a neutral notary can sit between marketplaces the way escrow.com sat on top of eBay. The cross-marketplace fraud graph becomes the moat.
first_30_days: Ship a free verification app and an MCP tool verify_task(task_id, evidence). Recruit ~200 witnesses in 3 cities. Pilot with two agent-errand marketplaces and five indie agent developers who hire humans for local pickups, at $1 per verification. Publish anonymized fraud statistics to establish credibility.

title: Independent Conformance Bench for CMS-0057-F APIs
one_liner: A testing-and-attestation service that runs the open-source Inferno and Da Vinci test kits against a health plan's real FHIR APIs and produces the evidence pack its compliance officer needs before January 2027.
customer: Small and mid-size Medicaid managed-care plans, regional Medicare Advantage plans, CHIP managed-care entities, TPAs and the small payer-IT vendors serving them. Buyer is the compliance officer or CIO who signed a vendor contract and can't verify it.
problem: CMS-0057-F requires four FHIR APIs (Patient Access, Provider Access, Payer-to-Payer, Prior Authorization) by 1 Jan 2027, and the 72-hour and 7-day decision timelines have applied since Jan 2026. Plans bought vendor stacks and hear 'we're compliant,' but the plan carries the liability. CMS points at ONC's Inferno tooling, yet almost no one independent runs it against the plan's production-like environment and writes the attestation.
solution: A managed test bench: Inferno with the Da Vinci PAS/CRD/DTR and CARIN test kits, Synthea synthetic members mapped to the plan's data model, latency and load tests aligned to the decision-time metrics, and SMART/OAuth security checks. Deliverables are a pass/fail matrix, remediation tickets for the vendor, an executive attestation binder, and quarterly regression runs as vendors ship updates.
why_now: Guidance is that plans commit to a stack by Q3 2026 to leave time for testing, so Q4 2026 is the test window. It is late September. The rule is fixed, the open-source test kits exist, and the buyers' vendors have a conflict of interest in grading themselves.
revenue_model: Fixed-fee readiness assessment of USD 15-40k. Quarterly regression subscription of USD 3-8k per month. Vendor-side 'independently tested' certification fee. Optional remediation project work.
non_obvious_insight: The buyer isn't engineering; it's a compliance officer who needs independent evidence to hold a vendor to account. Inferno has huge adoption among developers but has never been packaged as an auditor's deliverable. Independence, not tooling, is the product.
first_30_days: Spin up a hosted Inferno plus Synthea environment. Publish a free 'CMS-0057-F self-test cheat sheet.' Approach 10 Medicaid MCO compliance officers through state Medicaid association events and LinkedIn. Sell three pilot assessments at about USD 10k to build case studies before year-end. Partner with FHIR consultancies that lack independent status.

title: Meeting Subtext Captions for Neurodivergent Workers
one_liner: An on-screen coach for Zoom and Teams that flags conversational subtext (a question aimed at you, a topic shift, rising frustration) and supports post-meeting debriefs, sold through autism and ADHD coaches.
customer: Autism and ADHD coaching practices ($40-60 per client per month), employer neurodiversity hiring programs, and state vocational rehabilitation agencies.
problem: Autistic and ADHD adults often lose jobs and friendships over unspoken social subtext rather than skill. Human job coaches cost $75-150 an hour and cannot sit in every meeting. Loneliness among autistic adults is severe, and existing tools are scripts and courses that do not work in the live moment.
solution: A client-side app reading a live transcript and showing three private cue types ('direct question to you', 'time to wrap up', 'tone: irritated'), plus post-meeting debriefs shared with the coach and a rehearsal mode simulating hard meetings. Data stays local by default, and the coach dashboard shows patterns, not raw transcripts.
why_now: Real-time multimodal models now handle affect and conversational structure at low latency. Hybrid work makes meeting transcripts routine. Employers' neurodiversity hiring programs are maturing and need retention tools.
revenue_model: Per-seat license through coaching practices, employer accommodation budgets, and state vocational rehabilitation contracts.
non_obvious_insight: The right entry point is the coach's toolkit, not the consumer app. Coaches already have the trust, the payer relationship and the clinical framing, and AI extends their reach into moments they cannot attend.
first_30_days: Recruit 10 neurodiversity coaches through ADHD and autism coach networks. Pilot with 30 clients at $50 each, collect cue accuracy ratings and coach feedback, then approach two employers' neurodiversity leads.

title: Golden-Hour Payment Recall Desk for Small Firms
one_liner: A 24/7 retainer that runs the first 60 minutes after a fraudulent payment: bank fraud desks, recall requests and freeze filings, using a pre-built bank contact book.
customer: SMBs with 5-250 employees, sold through bookkeepers, CPAs, MSPs and crime-insurance brokers, at $99-299 per month. Insurers can subsidize.
problem: The FBI fund-freeze process handled 3,900 incidents ($1.16B attempted) and froze $679M, or 58%, yet individuals and SMBs rarely use it. BEC cost $3.05B and tech-support and takeover fraud $2.13B. One account takeover can fire 50+ ACH transfers to multiple banks, and victims lose the first hours to phone trees and confusion.
solution: At onboarding, capture bank fraud contacts and payment approvers. At incident time, a hotline and web intake runs the playbook: generate the IC3 complaint with the right fields, send correctly formatted ACH return and wire recall requests to sending and receiving banks, escalate to receiving-bank fraud teams, and assemble an evidence and insurance packet. Track which banks respond fastest.
why_now: IC3's 2025 report is the first to show freeze rates clearly, and instant rails have shrunk the window. Takeover cases are rising and shifting away from classic BEC.
revenue_model: Monthly retainer, $500-2,500 per incident, and insurer funding.
non_obvious_insight: The money is not gone in 24 hours: 58% of attempted funds froze when the process was used. The constraint is speed and paperwork, which is a service business. The moat is the bank response-time dataset that banks do not publish.
first_30_days: Sign 10 bookkeeping and MSP partners. Write the runbook and directory of top-50 bank fraud lines and 200 credit unions. Staff with two part-time ex-bank fraud analysts on rotation and pilot at $99 per month.

title: Short-Time Compensation as a Service
one_liner: Software and admin that lets employers shrink hours instead of headcount using state work-sharing programs, where unemployment insurance replaces part of the lost wages, as an alternative to AI-driven layoffs.
customer: HR and finance leaders at 50-2,000-employee firms in states with work-sharing programs (about half of US states, verify) planning 10-30% reductions in AI-exposed teams. PEOs and payroll providers are channels.
problem: Employers treat headcount cuts as binary, yet many states pay prorated UI when firms cut hours 10-60% rather than lay people off. Almost nobody uses it. AI-driven demand shifts are gradual and uncertain, layoffs risk rehire regret and severance costs, and workers lose health coverage and face 6-13 month searches.
solution: (1) A calculator comparing work-sharing to layoff, including severance, recruiting and regret costs. (2) Plan-filing automation per state. (3) Weekly claim administration integrated with payroll. (4) A training-hours module for reduced-hours periods. (5) Tracking of approvals and caps. (6) A glide path to natural attrition.
why_now: AI restructuring is happening under uncertainty (Challenger shows AI-cited cuts small and partly narrative), reversal headlines are growing, and the market is low-fire, low-hire, so retaining talent has become valuable.
revenue_model: $25-60 per participating employee per month, or 5-10% of validated avoided severance and rehire cost, plus PEO reseller revenue.
non_obvious_insight: The subsidy already exists and is unused because nobody owns the admin burden. Becoming the 'TurboTax for work-sharing' turns a public benefit into a retention and anti-regret hedge that contradicts the 'cut now' reflex.
first_30_days: Map work-sharing rules and forms in the 6-8 biggest states. Interview 15 mid-size HR leads and 5 PEOs. Offer free feasibility analyses to companies that filed WARN notices and convert 2-3 to paid pilots.

title: Cap Ledger for the 350-Home Rule
one_liner: An ownership graph that counts which LLCs a single-family rental owner controls, proves grandfathering and build-to-rent exemption, and becomes the audit trail lenders and buyers demand.
customer: SFR operators and funds with 100-2,000 homes (the almost-institutional tier), their lenders and securitization arrangers, and M&A counsel doing diligence.
problem: The ROAD to Housing Act caps institutional single-family-rental owners at 350 homes, exempts build-to-rent and grandfathers existing owners, but leaves key definitions and reporting mechanics unspecified. Owners hold homes through hundreds of LLCs and JVs, and nobody can currently prove a per-owner count, per-home acquisition date or build-to-rent status.
solution: Build a parcel-level ownership graph from county deeds, mailing addresses, secretary-of-state filings and mortgage records. Output each owner's 'cap position' plus a per-home evidence file (acquisition date, certificate-of-occupancy and first-lease date for BTR). A rules engine updates as regulations finalize, plus a 'what if I buy 60 more homes' scenario tool.
why_now: The cap and grandfathering are new, definitions are ambiguous, and every operator, lender and buyer suddenly needs a defensible number. Whoever's ledger regulators and counterparties adopt sets the standard.
revenue_model: $1-3 per home per year SaaS, $5-15K diligence packages per transaction, and lender portfolio-monitoring licenses.
non_obvious_insight: Insiders read the cap as a threat to institutional SFR, but a cap on new purchases makes grandfathered portfolios scarce capacity and makes provable status a balance-sheet asset. The graph also reveals 'independent' operators that are secretly affiliated, which is valuable to both sides. Sell the ledger, not a fixed reading of rules that will move.
first_30_days: Build the graph for two metros (for example Atlanta and Phoenix) from public deed data. Rank the top 50 owners and cold-email operators in the 100-1,000 home band with their own cap-position PDF. Convert 3 into $10K design-partner pilots. Retain an attorney to track rulemaking.

title: After-School Care Inside Senior Living Communities
one_liner: Turn senior living's empty afternoon dining rooms into licensed school-age programs where residents are reading, repair and garden 'buddies', funded by parent tuition, operator economics and loneliness-intervention budgets.
customer: Working parents of K-5 kids near independent- and assisted-living communities (dependent-care FSA eligible, cap $7,500). Secondary payers: senior living operators seeking occupancy and retention, and Medicare Advantage plans or Area Agencies on Aging funding loneliness programs.
problem: The 3-6pm care gap is where parents lose work hours, and average US childcare costs $13,128 (35% of income for single parents). Older adults are the least-served, highest-need loneliness segment, and 40-46% of adults 65+ are 'unsure' about AI companions (Pew, Aug 2026), so a human alternative has open ground. Operators have empty spaces between lunch and dinner and no scalable, reimbursable engagement model.
solution: 'Bridge Clubs': the community lends the room 2:30-6pm. We run a licensed school-age program (1:12 ratio, bus drop from the elementary school). Residents opt into structured 30-minute roles ('Reading Elders', 'Tinkerers', 'Garden Crew'). We track participation and a loneliness scale (UCLA-3) monthly and package the data for MA plans and AAAs so they can fund resident engagement. Parents pay less than typical after-school rates because space and volunteer time subsidize it.
why_now: The dependent-care FSA cap rose to $7,500 and the 45F employer childcare credit rose to 40% (50% for small businesses) in 2026, opening employer and parent budgets. WHO's 2025 Commission put loneliness on the health agenda. Payers are hunting for measurable loneliness interventions, and school-age licensing is lighter than infant care in many states.
revenue_model: Parent tuition of about $325-475/mo. Operator rent-share or management fee. Engagement-based fees from MA plans or AAAs. Employer sponsorship of slots via the 45F credit.
non_obvious_insight: This is two 'deserts' each holding the other's unused capacity. 'Intergenerational programming' usually fails as charity. It works when the payer stack (tuition, operator occupancy, and loneliness reimbursement) makes it profitable and the resident role is a job, not a photo op.
first_30_days: Find three independent-living operators within a mile of Title I elementary schools with after-school waitlists. Run a 6-week pilot with 12 kids in one dining room using a licensed partner provider. Charge $99 registration plus $349/mo. Collect resident participation and UCLA-3 scores. Take the data to one regional MA plan's community benefits team.

title: Positive Pay for Stablecoin Wallets
one_liner: Give mid-market finance teams the control environment auditors will demand before approving stablecoin flows: vendor wallet verification, sanctions and taint screening, and freeze-risk checks.
customer: Finance teams at $20M-$500M revenue companies starting to pay and receive USDC or USDT (via Citi and Coinbase, Stripe/Bridge or Circle), and the CPA and fractional-CFO firms that serve them.
problem: Stablecoin payments are irreversible, and wallet-address swaps and address poisoning are the new business email compromise. Companies inherit sanctions exposure (Senate Democrats allege about $2B of Iranian flows through Tether in a year). Funds received from a tainted wallet can be frozen. There is no bank-style 'positive pay' equivalent.
solution: Vendor wallet verification via signed challenge and callback, allowlist enforcement in the payment approval flow (Slack and email approvals), pre-payment counterparty screening, post-receipt taint checks, and NetSuite/QuickBooks reconciliation at the invoice level. Continuous behavioral KYC scoring, the gap flagged by The Block, is the roadmap.
why_now: Citi and Coinbase launched stablecoin acceptance with fiat settlement on 2026-09-28. Annual stablecoin volume tops $90T and doubled year on year, daily turnover is 0.78x, and the GENIUS Act takes effect around Jan 2027 (verify).
revenue_model: $500-$3,000 per month SaaS plus per-screen fees, sold through CPA and fractional-CFO channel partners.
non_obvious_insight: Corporate adoption is gated by the controller's control environment, not by wallets. Positive Pay is a large business in traditional banking, and the wallet analog doesn't exist. Whoever ships the audit-ready control set becomes the default checklist.
first_30_days: Interview 25 controllers and CFOs with live or planned stablecoin flows. Ship a browser extension plus Slack approvals for wallet verification and allowlists. Sell $299 per month pilots through five CPA firms serving importers and crypto-adjacent SMEs.

title: AI Coverage Buy-Back Packs for Insurance Agents
one_liner: An intake that turns a small business's AI usage into an underwriter-ready 'AI use and guardrails' package so its insurer will restore the coverage it just excluded.
customer: Independent insurance agencies and brokerages that serve SMBs, who pay per client pack or a monthly agency subscription. Their clients are marketing agencies, law and accounting firms, clinics, staffing firms and e-commerce brands that use AI heavily.
problem: ISO endorsements CG 40 47 and CG 40 48 took effect in January 2026 and let carriers exclude generative-AI-related bodily injury, property damage and advertising injury from standard general liability policies. Reporting says Chubb, Travelers and Berkshire Hathaway got state approvals, and more than 80% of such requests were approved. Absolute AI exclusions are also appearing on D&O and E&O policies, including for 'allegedly inadequate AI governance'. About 74% of small businesses already use AI tools, and agents cannot tell clients what evidence underwriters will accept.
solution: A 15-minute intake, plus an optional SSO or browser scan, inventories the client's AI tools. It maps each use (customer chatbot, AI-generated ads, AI hiring screens, AI note-takers with client data) to the coverage lines it touches. It then produces: (1) a coverage-gap report that flags CG 40 47/48 and absolute AI exclusions in the current policy, (2) an underwriter-ready AI use and guardrails statement with a human-review log and vendor list, and (3) a quote-request package aimed at markets that sell affirmative AI coverage or buy-backs. Every pack also gives the agent a talk track for the renewal meeting.
why_now: The exclusions have been in effect since January 2026 and are now hitting renewals. Search interest is rising in the underlying concepts: Exploding Topics shows AI Guardrails +8,400%, Responsible AI +3,600% and Cyber Insurance +763%. Colorado's AI Act, delayed to Jan 1, 2027, and Illinois HB 3773 (in effect Jan 1, 2026) add employer-side documentation duties that the same pack can reuse.
revenue_model: $149-$299 per client pack, or $199-$499/month per agency for unlimited packs plus renewal reminders. Later: a referral or placement fee from managing general agents and carriers that write AI buy-backs, and a co-branded version sold through carrier appointment programs.
non_obvious_insight: The evidence standard does not exist yet. Law firm analyses of the exclusions note they 'stop short of prescribing specific governance standards insurers will accept' (https://www.lathropgpm.com/insights/the-ai-coverage-gap-what-new-insurance-exclusions-mean-for-your-business/) and describe fragmenting coverage across GL, D&O, E&O and EPLI (https://www.fenwick.com/insights/publications/end-silent-ai-emerging-ai-exclusions-coverage-fragmentation-and-practical-implications). Whichever evidence format two or three underwriters or MGAs accept first will become the SOC 2 of AI coverage. Agents, not the businesses themselves, are the right buyer because they lose commission if a client goes bare. Cyber-insurance search interest is up 763% and AI Guardrails up 8,400% (https://explodingtopics.com/finance-topics, https://explodingtopics.com/blog/trending-topics), which shows SMBs are already looking for this without a product to buy.
first_30_days: Days 1-10: build the intake form and PDF generator, and interview 15 independent agents (local IIABA and Big I chapters, LinkedIn) about how renewals with AI exclusions are being handled. Days 11-20: run free packs for each agent's five most AI-heavy clients, and ask two MGA underwriters whether the format is acceptable. Days 21-30: start charging $149 per pack. Target 5 agencies at $199/month and post 'we got X's AI coverage bought back' cases from the pilots.

title: Pattern-Less Foundry Network via Printed Sand Molds
one_liner: Print sand molds centrally and pour them at idle small foundries to deliver castings in about two weeks with no patterns.
customer: Pump, valve, ag-equipment and machinery OEMs and repair shops needing 5-500 castings. Small foundries are the supply side.
problem: Small-lot castings from Asia now face tariffs and freight up to 50% higher. Domestic foundries quote long lead times, largely because of pattern-making and minimum runs, and aging owners are retiring or closing. Castings are an invisible bottleneck under reshoring and under Section 232 derivative rates.
solution: A hub with binder-jet sand printing (or rented capacity at existing bureaus) prints mold and core packages from customer CAD plus solidification simulation. Ship them to 10-30 small foundries that pour iron, steel or aluminum. The network handles NDT, dimensional checks and certs, including melt origin. Start with one or two alloys and repair and replacement parts.
why_now: Printed sand has improved in cost and speed, tariffs and freight punish imported castings, foundries are consolidating, and simulation and AI gating design are cheap.
revenue_model: Per-casting pricing with 25-35% gross margin. $500-3k engineering fee per part. Foundries pay for mold volume routed to them.
non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck is patterns and scheduling, not melting. Many small foundries have idle furnace hours but no digital front door, and a printed mold is a universal interface. US-melt certification is a sales kicker, not the core.
first_30_days: Sign three foundries with idle capacity. Buy printed molds from an existing bureau. Take 10 orders for obsolete pump or gearbox housings at $1-3k each, using 3D scans of broken parts.

title: Whale-Proof Alert Network for Longline Boats
one_liner: A reciprocal, location-fuzzed alert network that lets sablefish and halibut longliners warn each other about orcas and sperm whales without giving up their fishing spots.
customer: Owner-operators of IFQ longline vessels in the Gulf of Alaska, Southeast and Bering Sea (roughly several hundred boats), sold through fishermen's associations, at $600-1,500 per vessel per season. Expansion buyers are pelagic longline fleets worldwide (tuna, toothfish) that also lose fish to whales.
problem: Whales strip the gear as it comes up, and bad sets lose a double-digit percentage of the catch. The whales learn the sound of your hauler and follow the boat, and sometimes the fleet. Every skipper knows it, but sightings travel only on private VHF codes and phone calls. Reporting a whale reveals where you are fishing. The boat that 'brings the whales' gets blamed. So the fleet's best early-warning data is never pooled.
solution: An app and text-message bot that runs over Garmin inReach, Iridium or Starlink. A skipper sends a one-line report ('killer whales, 8 mi of hall X'). The system publishes only a fuzzed geohash after a delay and strips vessel identity. You can see alerts only if you report (reciprocity credits). A model adds depredation-risk scores by area, soak time, season and haul timing. A playbook covers acoustic hygiene: hauler noise, set and haul timing, gear moves. An optional hydrophone kit comes later. Anonymized data goes to researchers, associations and insurers.
why_now: Quotas are tight and sablefish and halibut prices are well below their highs, so every whale-eaten pound matters more. Satellite texting from the wheelhouse is now cheap and near-universal (Starlink, inReach). Researchers have shown that whales learn from boat acoustics, which gives the fleet a reason to trust a shared system. Fishermen have also been moving toward pots to cope with whales, which shows they will pay for anything that works.
revenue_model: Per-vessel seasonal subscription ($600-1,500), association-level enterprise licenses, and anonymized depredation data sold to research programs, regulators and insurers. Upside is global pelagic longline fleets that all have the same depredation problem.
non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck is not detection technology, it is mechanism design. Skippers guard spots and fear blame, so they share whale sightings only in private. A network that gives value only to reporters, blurs location and time, and hides identity solves that. It is a game-theory product disguised as a whale app. Whale behavior is also fleet-learned, so tracking anonymized boat signatures over time is a data asset nobody else has.
first_30_days: Recruit 25 skippers in Sitka, Kodiak and Homer through the longline associations. The sablefish season closes mid-November, so use the winter to run it as a manual pilot: a group text plus a spreadsheet plus a simple map, paying $100 for reports. Interview skippers about how they signal each other today. Draft the fuzzing rules with them. Sell pre-season subscriptions in Feb-Mar and go live for the March opening.

title: Indonesia Halal Rescue for Food Exporters
one_liner: A fast-track service that gets mid-size food, supplement and cosmetics exporters registered and documented under Indonesia's mandatory halal regime, then keeps them compliant.
customer: Mid-size US, EU and Australian exporters and their Indonesian importers, plus halal certifiers who white-label the work.
problem: Halal certification becomes mandatory for imported food, beverages, cosmetics and supplements on 17 Oct 2026, with enforcement from 18 Oct. The authority says no extensions, certification takes 3-6 months, and USDA FAS (Sept 2026) flags roughly $2.5B of US ag exports affected. Many mid-size firms treat halal as a marketing label and have not started.
solution: A gap analysis, supplier halal-declaration collection, matching to recognized foreign halal bodies, registration filing, and label and claim review. A software ledger tracks every ingredient and supplier certificate across SKUs and alerts on expiry, which also serves kosher and EU documentation needs.
why_now: The cliff is three weeks away and the lead time exceeds that, so late movers face shipment holds. After the deadline the work shifts to cure (relabeling, re-filing, clearing stuck shipments), which is recurring.
revenue_model: $4-15k per SKU-family project plus $500-2k/month monitoring, and certifier white-label fees.
non_obvious_insight: Halal has become a customs gate rather than a marketing certificate, so budgets come from logistics and compliance, not brand. The ingredient-and-supplier documentation ledger is reusable across regimes.
first_30_days: Email and LinkedIn outreach to 300 exporters from USDA export directories and state trade offices, offering a $750 48-hour readiness check. Partner with 1-2 recognized halal bodies and prioritize firms with shipments already in transit.

title: Duty Refund Claims Desk for Small Importers
one_liner: Over $100B in tariff refunds are flowing, but small importers can't afford the paperwork. Run the filing, deadline tracking and refund advance as a service.
customer: Small and mid importers of record ($1M-$50M of annual imports) that paid the struck-down tariffs, plus customs brokers who don't want the grunt work.
problem: Refunds are flowing but small importers face records, liquidation and protest deadlines, multiple brokers and bonds, and filing costs ('not without a cost,' Colorado Sun, 2026-07-02). The government is fighting an order to refund all importers (WaPo, 2026-08-11). Brokers are paid per entry, not per refund, so nobody chases.
solution: Connect customs-entry data from the importer's broker, identify eligible entries and deadlines, file protests and post-summary corrections through a partner licensed customs broker, and track each claim to payment. Offer an advance of about 80% of approved claims at a discount, funded by a small credit facility.
why_now: Refunds have passed $100B (CNBC 2026-08-07, Forbes 2026-09-09) with litigation ongoing. Twenty-five states are challenging the replacement Section 122 tariffs, so a second claim wave may follow.
revenue_model: 10-15% success fee on recovered duties, plus a 2-3% monthly discount on advances once financing is in place.
non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck isn't law, it's data assembly and deadline hygiene. The refund often lands in a broker's account or gets stuck for lack of a clear owner. Small importers who recover cash are also the source of pass-through claims for the downstream-recovery business.
first_30_days: Sign a licensed customs broker as partner. Recruit 20 importers through marketplace-seller communities and manufacturer associations. Process five entries by hand end to end and collect the first success fees.

title: Mahjong Leagues for Senior Living Communities
one_liner: A turnkey mahjong program (kits, instructors, scoring app, inter-community leagues) sold to senior-living activity directors.
customer: Activity directors at independent and assisted living communities (roughly 30k in the US), 55+ HOAs, and library systems.
problem: Mahjong is booming: CNN (19 Sept 2026) covers the explosion, Yelp searches for mahjong clubs rose about 4,467% in 2025, and the National Mah Jongg League reports 350k+ members. Coverage frames it as a Gen Z and millennial aesthetic trend. Meanwhile senior-living calendars need social, cognitive, low-injury weekly activities, and American mahjong is hard to learn and hard to staff with teachers.
solution: A subscription with a 4-table starter kit, certified instructor visits (in person or video), monthly inter-community league nights with a shared leaderboard and trophy, a coordinator app, and staff training so the community can run it alone.
why_now: The mainstream boom is producing demand and a supply of instructors from the new club scene. Pickleball injuries make low-impact alternatives attractive for the same age group.
revenue_model: $300-600/month per community, $250 kits, per-visit instructor fees, and tile-maker sponsorships.
non_obvious_insight: Tile brands and influencers chase young buyers with $200 designer sets. The recurring money sits with older players who play weekly and with institutions that have a budget line called 'activities'. Inter-facility leagues create retention and sales compounding, because a community that joins forces its rivals to join.
first_30_days: Approach 20 senior communities in one metro via activity-director networks. Run free two-week pilots staffed by 2 volunteer instructors recruited from local clubs. Convert 5 into $300/month accounts and stage the first inter-community match.

title: Flood Closing Desk for Title Agents
one_liner: A day-one flood file on every purchase: elevation, zone challenge, private flood substitute and NFIP-lapse fallback.
customer: Title and escrow agencies and mortgage brokers in coastal and riverine markets, with contingency fees from homeowners.
problem: NFIP authority expires Sept 30 2026 after more than 30 short-term extensions. In the 2010 lapse about 1,400 closings a day were delayed or cancelled (secondary source). Even without a lapse, zone and elevation problems surface on day 25 of a 30-day contract, and premiums must roughly double toward full risk.
solution: An order-time 'Flood File': LiDAR-derived elevation, zone confirmation, candidates for a Letter of Map Amendment, an instant private-flood quote with a compliance letter as an NFIP substitute during lapses, and a Risk Rating 2.0 estimate. Title agencies embed it in their order flow.
why_now: Authority lapses in two days, and premium glide-path increases make every flood file a live cost.
revenue_model: $95-250 per file, $500-1,500 contingency for successful zone removal, and private flood placement commission.
non_obvious_insight: Buyers and lenders pay to avoid closing delays. Zone challenges are an arbitrage, since a successful removal saves the owner premiums every year.
first_30_days: Contract with 5 title offices, partner with a surveyor, hand-deliver 100 files, and track removal success rates.

title: Chute-Side Cow Counts for Ag Lenders
one_liner: Turn the vet's preg-check clipboard into a borrower-consented, third-party-verified herd inventory that banks can lend against.
customer: Community banks, Farm Credit associations and ag lenders with cattle loan books (they require it or pay per report, usually passed through to the borrower). Secondary payer is the cow-calf or heifer-development operator who wants bigger operating lines or bred-heifer financing on better terms.
problem: Cattle collateral has no VIN. Lenders verify with drive-by counts and borrower-supplied spreadsheets, and prosecutors in 2026 alleged a roughly $9.4M fraud that included a loan of $2.8M against 850 head. Farm loan delinquencies are rising while bred cows trade around $3,000+ per head, so a 500-cow borrower is $1.5M+ of collateral that nobody independent has counted.
solution: A 'Verified Herd Report' generated at the working day the vet is already doing. The vet or tech logs every head with an EID or visual tag scan (a $500 handheld reader plus a phone app), age class, pregnancy status and stage, and location. The vet e-signs and the borrower approves sharing with one tap. The lender gets a portal with timestamped, geotagged counts and year-over-year flags (head count down, pregnancy rate down, tags not matching last year). A second light pass happens at weaning. The vet earns a per-head fee for data they already write down and throw in the truck door pocket.
why_now: Federal EID ear tags became mandatory for many interstate cattle movements in Nov 2024, so per-head digital ID is now normal and cheap. Herd rebuilding at record cattle prices is being financed with debt, lenders entered 2026 carrying operating losses from 2023-2025 (rising delinquencies and restructures), and a fresh cattle-collateral fraud case is making ag loan committees ask for verification. Fall preg-check season is running right now (Sept-Nov).
revenue_model: $2-3 per head per verification, split roughly 50/50 with the vet practice, charged to the borrower or the lender as a loan condition. Add a portfolio dashboard for lenders at $500-2,000 per month once an institution has 100+ verified borrowers. Later, sell the verified inventory and pregnancy data to lenders as an underwriting input (advance rates on verified bred heifers).
non_obvious_insight: The vet is the only independent professional who physically handles every animal in the herd once or twice a year. They count, tag-check and pregnancy-check every cow, and that data dies on a clipboard. Vets refuse to police clients, but they will happily attest to what they handled when the borrower initiates the request, so the conflict-of-interest problem disappears. Honest borrowers are the real buyers: verified bred females can justify higher advance rates, and that cheap capital funds the fee many times over.
first_30_days: Preg-check season is live, so sign up 3 rural practices that each do several thousand head of fall preg-checks. Pitch 3-4 community-bank ag lenders (target the one who has been burned by a herd count before; work through state bankers' association ag committees). Run a pilot on about 10 willing borrowers with a form-based app and a PDF report, charging $2/head. Gather a before and after on what the lender learned that the drive-by inspection missed, then use that to sell the annual program.

title: Conversion X-Ray: Scan and Warrant Hidden Risks
one_liner: A 10-day scan of vacant office buildings (LiDAR, ground-penetrating radar, riser mapping) with an AI cost-risk budget, evolving into a cost-overrun warranty backed by the data.
customer: Buyers of distressed office evaluating conversion, their construction and mezzanine lenders, and later sureties and insurers.
problem: Conversions fail on unknowns: slab thickness and post-tension cables, asbestos and fireproofing, riser locations, window operability, structural transfers. Buyers price with averages and blow budgets by 20-40%, and lenders demand large contingencies or refuse.
solution: A rapid package for 40-300k sf buildings: handheld or drone LiDAR, GPR on slabs, facade thermal imaging, MEP riser mapping and sample testing. An AI cost-risk model outputs a per-unit cost distribution and a P80 budget in 10 days. As actual-versus-predicted data accumulates, offer a warranty or overrun cover.
why_now: $39B of office debt matures within 12 months and the buyer pool needs faster diligence. Handheld SLAM LiDAR and vision models are cheap, and public-land and affordable conversions require cost certainty.
revenue_model: $0.30-0.90 per sf for the scan, later warranty premiums of 1-2% of hard cost or lender-paid programs.
non_obvious_insight: Every conversion overrun is a data point that nobody collects. The first firm to log predicted-versus-actual cost across 50 conversions owns the only actuarial dataset in a market that insurers cannot yet price, so the scan is the loss leader for an insurance-like margin.
first_30_days: Buy a handheld LiDAR and rent a GPR unit. Scan three buildings at a discount for buyers in bid periods. Publish 'the top 10 hidden conversion killers' and sign two paid scans at about $15K each.

title: Hard-Stop Fuse and Warranty for AI Cloud Bills
one_liner: A free scanner finds unrestricted legacy Google/Firebase and Bedrock exposure, installs a real hard kill-switch, and later sells a capped bill-shock warranty only to accounts that have the fuse installed.
customer: Seed-stage startups, solo developers and small agencies running LLM calls on GCP/Firebase or AWS Bedrock, including anyone running coding agents unattended. They pay $29-49/month per cloud account for the fuse and monitoring, and a small warranty premium later.
problem: Cloud providers ship alerts and credits, not hard caps, and they often refuse refunds. A Bedrock user ran up $37,901.73 through a LiteLLM + prompt-caching miss and asked 'why can I not say this IAM principal may spend at most $200/month'. A 2016 Firebase Android key generated $67k of Gemini charges in 19 hours, and Google support said it was 'unable to make adjustments'. A Claude Code user burned $2,000+ without noticing. A founder's $4,200 fraudulent Gemini charge was followed by suspension of a $1M ARR company's whole Google Cloud project.
solution: Step 1, a read-only CLI/web scanner that lists unrestricted API keys, projects with Gemini or Bedrock enabled, forgotten legacy Firebase keys (which the May 2024 auto-restriction policy missed in at least one documented case), and missing budget actions. Step 2, a one-click installer for hard stops: key restrictions and quota overrides on GCP, and on AWS Budget Actions that attach an IAM/SCP deny on model invocation. Step 3, per-minute anomaly detection that trips the fuse in seconds, not at the next daily billing rollup. Step 4, once an account has run fused for 30+ days, a capped bill-shock warranty (start at $5k, backed by a small reserve, later an MGA or reinsurer) priced from the loss data the fuse collects.
why_now: Unattended agents with huge contexts and Opus-class pricing turned ordinary integration mistakes into five-figure invoices in 2026. Gemini access now hangs off keys created years before Gemini existed. Google and AWS are visibly not shipping hard caps: the April 2026 $67k Gemini case was denied adjustment as of May 2026, and the $37.9k Bedrock case is from April 2026.
revenue_model: Free scan (lead gen). $29/month per cloud account for fuse plus monitoring, $49 for multi-project agencies. $199 one-off audit-and-install for agencies. Warranty add-on priced at roughly 2-4% of the covered limit per year, sold only to fused accounts.
non_obvious_insight: The clouds have shown the market will not get hard caps or reliable refunds from them, so the insurable unit is a fused account, not a customer. The technical control doubles as underwriting, and every victim thread is a warm lead. Evidence: $37,901.73 Bedrock bill with the 'hard spend limit' complaint https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47933355; $67k in 19 hours with Google denying adjustment and other victims reporting $13,000 and £2,700 https://discuss.ai.google.dev/t/unexpected-67k-gemini-api-spike-in-19-hours-2016-firebase-provisioned-android-key-not-covered-by-googles-may-2024-auto-restriction-policy/142717; $1M ARR startup suspended after a compromised key https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48396596; $2,000+ Claude Code invoice https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46851021. Caveat: refunds are not reliably obtainable, so do not lead with a claims-desk model.
first_30_days: Week 1-2: build the GCP key/Gemini exposure scanner on top of Cloud Asset Inventory and publish 'Check your 2016 Firebase keys' on HN and the Google AI forum thread. Week 3: add an AWS CloudFormation one-click Budget Action deny for Bedrock. Week 4: DM the authors and repliers of the public bill-shock threads, plus agencies, and offer a $199 audit-and-install to the first 20; convert them to $29/month monitoring. Log every trip event and near-miss to build the actuarial base for the warranty.
